question.:question/worked-solution:
This integral resembles the basic integral for inverse tangent,

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+{u}^{2}}\text{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}⁡u+C.
$$

The only difference is that instead of ${u}^{2}$ as the variable, we have $64{x}^{2}=(8x)^{2}.$

So, let's substitute $u=8x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=8\,⟹\,\frac{1}{8}\,\text{d}u=\text{d}x.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{1+64{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{1+(8x)^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{1+{u}^{2}}\,\cdot (\frac{1}{8}\text{d}u) \\  & =\frac{1}{8}\int \frac{1}{1+{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{8}\operatorname{arctan}⁡u+C \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{arctan}⁡(8x)}{8}+C\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
